_about: Order 14 builder C (19 Nov 2026): THE FIXED CONTRACT CHECKLIST, used on every contract review IN ADDITION to the checklist written from the held standards (`aim_review.contract_code.checklist_items`). Each item says what to check and who decides it: 'code' = code compares the paper's own verified quotes (`aim_review.contract_code.lines`); 'judge' = the AI judge reads it (an item not from a held standard: never Met or Not met, an AI opinion or a Question); 'code+judge' = code decides the part named in `code_part`, the judge reads the rest. Reuses the KINDS of the earlier draft CT-01..CT-08 (`reference/contract_checks.json`, read only by `scripts/contract_checks.py`, not on the review path). AI draft: an engineer confirms it. Written from general contract practice, never from one paper's text.

items.check: Every party is named in full with its legal form, registration and address; the defined name of each party (in brackets or quotes) is used for it throughout; no party is left as a blank or a placeholder at signing.
The execution block has a signatory, title and date for every party; the effective date is stated or tied to a stated event; blanks to be filled at signing are listed as such.
The work is described or tied to a named Schedule that describes it; the scope sentence does not leave the work undefined.
The price is stated with its currency, the type of price (lump sum, rates) is clear, and the Schedule that sets it out is named.
items.code_part: an amount in words and the same amount in figures in one quote agree, and the currency in words matches the currency code (`amount_words`)

items.check: Invoicing, the paying currency, payment days and the stages or milestones of payment are stated and add up to the whole price.
items.code_part: a split of percentages that says 'equally' has equal parts; a split adds up to 100 (`splits`)

items.topic: Securities: retention, performance and advance payment bonds
items.check: Each security states its amount (percentage and base), who issues it, when it is given and when it is returned; a rate and a cap of the same security agree everywhere they are stated.
items.code_part: two different percentages for the same thing (same clause heading, same base and the same kind of statement: a rate or a cap) (`percent_values`); a percentage in words and in figures agree (`amount_words`)

items.check: Delay (liquidated) damages state a rate, its base, the period it runs per, and a cap; the cap sits inside the overall liability cap.
items.code_part: a rate per day or week times the stated maximum number of days or weeks against the stated cap of the same clause (`delay_cap`)

items.check: The start date, the completion date and the stated duration agree; the completion date is after the start.
items.code_part: end before start; start plus the stated duration against the stated end date, unambiguous date forms only (`dates`)

items.check: The warranty period, its start event and the remedy for defects are stated, and the release of retention or securities is tied to it consistently.
The contractor may assign, transfer or subcontract only with the company's prior written consent; any exception is stated.
The grounds for termination by each party, the notice period and the payment on termination are stated or tied to a named Schedule.
One governing law is named, or the Schedule that names it; it does not conflict with the place of disputes or the agents named for notices.
The way disputes are settled (negotiation, arbitration, courts), its seat and rules are stated or tied to a named Schedule, and notices of referral go to agents in a place consistent with it.
Notices are in writing, the means of delivery and addresses of both parties are stated, and a language or form rule does not contradict the rest of the contract.
The HSE requirements are stated or tied to a named Schedule that is part of the contract.
The quality requirements are stated or tied to a named Schedule that is part of the contract.
Any local content, in-country value or local workforce requirement is stated or tied to a named Schedule or attachment.

items.topic: Contract documents and order of precedence
items.check: Every Schedule the order of precedence ranks is a listed part of the contract and every listed Schedule is ranked; each is held in the package; one Schedule is ranked once.
items.code_part: precedence list against the list of Schedules, both ways, and against the held package (`schedules`)

items.check: A term the contract defines is used in its defined form throughout.
items.code_part: a defined term written with a different capitalisation (`terms`): a Question, never a verdict
